questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
Which labels might be used on a production possibility curve diagram? Y (vertical) axis X (horizontal) axis

options.A: capital input labour input
options.B: cost of production quantity produced
options.C: output of rice labour input
options.D: output of rice output of sugar

questions.questionText: A good’s defining quality is that its consumption by one person prevents its consumption by someone else. How is this good classified?

options.A: a free good
options.B: a non-excludable good
options.C: a non-rival good
options.D: a private good

questions.questionText: Which is a normative economic statement?

options.A: Money is the least liquid form of wealth.
options.B: Some firms are subsidised by the government.
options.C: Some workers earn more than others.
options.D: Taxes are the best way to discourage smoking.

questions.questionText: The price of a ticket for an international athletics tournament was $50. All tickets were sold. Which area on the diagram represents consumer surplus? supply price per DZ ticket ($) C B

options.A: demand quantity (thousands)

questions.questionText: Market demand curves normally slope downwards. They may also shift from D to either D or D .
What is not a function of the price mechanism?

options.A: to act as a signal to firms when allocating resources
options.B: to maximise consumer surplus
options.C: to provide an incentive to firms to produce goods
options.D: to ration scarce resources

questions.questionText: A government introduces a maximum price above the market price. What will be the effect on consumer and producer surplus? consumer surplus producer surplus

options.A: fall rise
options.B: rise fall
options.C: rise unchanged
options.D: unchanged unchanged

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for air travel in Asia. The initial market equilibrium is at X. What will be the new equilibrium if the price of aviation fuel rises and incomes are falling in Asia? price of S 3 air travel S

options.B: S
options.A: X C D D
options.D: 1 O quantity of air travel

questions.questionText: A government increased a specific tax on shoes. The resulting increase in the price of shoes was paid mainly by the consumer and not by the producer. What must be true for this to happen?

options.A: The price elasticity of demand was less than the price elasticity of supply.
options.B: The price elasticity of demand was unitary.
options.C: The price elasticity of supply was less than one.
options.D: The price elasticity of supply was inelastic while the price elasticity of demand was elastic.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows supply and demand for a good. The original equilibrium is X. What will be the new equilibrium if subsidies are given to firms for new machinery? S price B S S

options.C: 2 A X D D D D O quantity

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for a normal good. price S D O quantity What is likely to cause both demand and supply curves to shift to the right?

options.A: a fall in the price of the good and a fall in the rate of indirect tax on the good
options.B: a rise in the price of a complementary good and an increase in the number of firms in the industry
options.C: a rise in the price of a substitute good and a fall in the price of a raw material used in the production of the good
options.D: an improvement in production techniques and a fall in the incomes of consumers

questions.questionText: The diagrams relate to the markets for four different products. In which market would a 10% decrease in demand and simultaneously a 10% increase in supply definitely result in both a fall in equilibrium price and a rise in equilibrium quantity?

options.A: B S S price price D D O O quantity quantity
options.C: D D S price price S D O O quantity quantity

questions.questionText: Why might governments provide free education for children aged 4 to 16 years old?

options.A: Consumers are not fully aware of the benefits of education.
options.B: Education in a free market system would be over consumed.
options.C: Education is a public good and there would be many free riders.
options.D: The private costs of education exceed the private benefits in a free market.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows three possible tax schemes. X tax paid Y Z O personal income What can be concluded about these tax schemes?

options.A: X is more progressive than Z.
options.B: X, Y and Z are all proportional.
options.C: Y is the only proportional tax.
options.D: Z is more regressive than Y.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an initial market equilibrium for an agricultural product of $6 and 800 units. S price 10 ($) D 0 400 800 quantity How much will the government have to spend to increase the market price to $10?

The table identifies items of government annual spending. $ million army pay 35 civil servants’ salaries 125 farming subsidies 15 pension payments 75 welfare benefits 50 What is the total government expenditure on transfer payments?
A subsidy is given to the producers of a good with perfectly elastic demand. What will be the outcome?

options.A: Consumer and producer receive equal amounts of subsidy.
options.B: There will be no change in price; the incidence of the subsidy will fall on the producer.
options.C: There will be a large increase in quantity consumed; the incidence of the subsidy will fall on the consumer.
options.D: There will be no change in the quantity consumed; the incidence of the subsidy will fall on the consumer.

questions.questionText: ‘Primary income’ and ‘secondary income’ are components of the current account of the balance of payments. What do these represent? primary income secondary income

options.A: capital flows financial flows
options.B: goods balance services balance
options.C: income flows current transfers
options.D: private flows government flows

What is not an example of protectionism?

options.A: the European Union (EU) requiring goods imported into member states to meet safety standards
options.B: the Pakistan government increasing the rate of goods and services tax, GST, on some exported goods from 2% to 5%
options.C: the Nigeria government banning the import of packaged sugar
options.D: the US imposing a 35% tariff on tyres imported from China

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual percentage increases in a country’s consumer prices index (CPI). year % change 2015 8.3 2016 6.0 2017 6.0 2018 1.0 Which statement is correct?

options.A: Consumer prices, on average, fell throughout the period.
options.B: Consumer prices, on average, remained the same in 2016 and 2017.
options.C: The general level of consumer prices was at its highest in 2015.
options.D: The general level of consumer prices was at its highest in 2018.

questions.questionText: The table indicates the factor inputs required to produce wheat and cars in countries X and Y. units of factor units of factor inputs to produce inputs to produce one tonne of wheat one car country X 4 2 country Y 8 6 What makes it possible for both countries to benefit from trade?

options.A: Country X has an absolute advantage in wheat and car production.
options.B: Country Y has an absolute advantage in wheat and car production.
options.C: Country Y has a comparative advantage in wheat production.
options.D: Opportunity cost of wheat and car production is the same between countries.

questions.questionText: In February 2016 the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) urged major economies such as the US and Japan to increase government spending. How would this affect the aggregate demand (AD) curve in these countries?

options.A: a move left along the AD curve
options.B: a move right along the AD curve
options.C: a move to the left of the AD curve
options.D: a move to the right of the AD curve

questions.questionText: A foreign government pays a UK university to educate its students. How would this be recorded on the balance of payments current account of the UK? current account money flows component

options.A: secondary income inflow
options.B: secondary income outflow
options.C: trade in services inflow
options.D: trade in services outflow

questions.questionText: The tables show changes over a period in the average prices of a country’s exports and imports. They are expressed as index numbers, with year 0 as 100. index of export prices index of import prices year 0 year 1 year 2 year 0 year 1 year 2 100 115 125 100 120 125 What is the change in the country’s terms of trade index between years 1 and 2?

options.A: It improves by about 10%.
options.B: It improves between 4% and 5%.
options.C: It stays the same.
options.D: It worsens between 4% and 5%.

questions.questionText: Which aim would be consistent with a government’s decision to buy its own currency in foreign exchange markets?

options.A: an appreciation under a freely floating exchange rate system
options.B: an appreciation under a managed float exchange rate system
options.C: a depreciation under a fixed exchange rate system
options.D: a devaluation under a managed float exchange rate system

questions.questionText: Which policy would assist in reducing a deficit within the balance of payments?

options.A: increasing interest rates
options.B: increasing the money supply
options.C: reducing subsidies to exporting industries
options.D: reducing the level of direct taxation
